reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows that W addition increases hardness and strength in VCrFeTaxWx alloys via lattice distortion, but it also states that W promotes a secondary BCC2 phase and Ta promotes Laves phases, which directly contradicts the premise that 5 at.% W will maintain a single-phase BCC structure in TiVNbTa. No evidence is provided for the specific TiVNbTa system, the 5 at.% threshold, or the retention of ductility.
premises: Adding W to a BCC HEA increases solid-solution strengthening via atomic size mismatch and lattice distortion.
This strengthening mechanism remains effective at elevated temperatures (up to 1273 K).
~5 at.% W addition to TiVNbTa will not induce detrimental secondary phases (e.g., Laves phase) and will maintain a single-phase BCC structure.
The resulting alloy will have improved high-temperature yield/compressive strength with only minor ductility loss.
